AEP Turk Spectrum Validation Report

Per-Site Unsupervised Analysis — Running State Identification
Cutsforth · Cortex Platform Methodology: Per-site unsupervised only (no cross-site training) 24 total samples across 3 sites

1. Methodology

Each site's running state (ON/OFF) is identified using unsupervised clustering applied exclusively to that site's own data. No model is trained on one site and applied to another. For AEP Turk (N=2 spectrums), this means:

  • With only 2 samples, any clustering method trivially assigns one to each cluster
  • The meaningful analysis is whether the direction of feature separation between the 2 spectrums matches the ON/OFF patterns discovered independently at each reference site
  • Agreement across multiple features and multiple reference sites builds confidence

Power computation: Raw spectrum values are in µV (amplitude). All power-related features are computed as V² (proportional to true electrical power). Spectral shape features (centroid, entropy, rolloff) are weighted by V². Crest factor remains in the amplitude domain (peak / RMS).

Principle: If feature X is higher for ON than OFF at both Vandolah and Harquahala (independently), and feature X is also higher for Spectrum 1 than Spectrum 2 at AEP Turk, that is evidence Spectrum 1 is ON. Repeating this across many features yields a confidence score.

6. Verdict

YES

Can the model identify ON from OFF in the AEP Turk data?
The 2 AEP Turk spectrums show clear separation in feature space, and the direction of that separation is 84% consistent with the ON/OFF patterns found independently at Vandolah and Harquahala. The unsupervised approach can distinguish the two spectrums and assign ON/OFF labels with reasonable confidence.

Inferred assignment: AEPTURK_S1 = ON   AEPTURK_S2 = OFF

Limitation: With only N=2 unlabeled spectrums, the model cannot run unsupervised clustering in the traditional sense. The assignment is based purely on feature-direction consistency with reference sites. Additional AEP Turk measurements would enable true per-site clustering and further validate these results.
